description:
Advances: specled.package

priv/spec_init/agents/skills/spec-led-development/SKILL.md.eex:120 describes mix spec.status as "Read-only." That is false: it executes enabled kind-command verification targets BY DEFAULT. This file is scaffolded by mix spec.init into every adopting repo, so specled ships the false belief to its users. Full evidence in the first comment.

comments.text:
EVIDENCE — verified by execution twice, independently, during epic specled_-i4x.

The false line, priv/spec_init/agents/skills/spec-led-development/SKILL.md.eex:120:

    - `mix spec.status` — coverage summary, weak spots, ADR usage. Read-only.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. Exactly TWO tasks execute repo-authored command targets by default:

  lib/mix/tasks/spec.status.ex:77-82   report_run_commands?/1  {:ok, false} -> false; _ -> true
  lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:180-185  same shape

Only two are genuinely opt-in:

  lib/mix/tasks/spec.prime.ex:87-90    {:ok, value} -> value; :error -> false
  lib/mix/tasks/spec.validate.ex:69    opts[:run_commands] || false

Measured with a fixture repo carrying one subject with a kind: command / execute: true target whose
command appends a line to an absolute sentinel path; sentinel deleted before each run. Two different
cold agents built their own fixtures and got the same result:

  mix spec.status --root FIX                     -> sentinel WRITTEN   (executes)
  mix spec.status --root FIX --no-run-commands   -> sentinel empty
  mix spec.check  --root FIX                     -> sentinel WRITTEN   (documented)
  mix spec.validate --root FIX                   -> sentinel empty     (opt-in, correct)
  mix spec.prime  --root FIX                     -> sentinel empty     (opt-in, correct)
  mix spec.next / spec.index / spec.review / spec.triangle --root FIX -> sentinel empty

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A DOC NIT. Verification targets are plain strings parsed out of
repo-resident .spec/specs/*.spec.md. The only gate is runnable_command_verification?/1
(lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2766-2772): kind, execute: true, non-empty target, covers is a list of
binaries. No syntax inspection, no allowlist. The target is then interpolated verbatim into a
/bin/sh script and spawned via Port.open (verifier.ex:2331-2352).

So an adopter who trusts the "Read-only." line and puts mix spec.status in a fork-PR CI lane
executes attacker-authored shell with that job's token. Because this file ships via mix spec.init,
the misleading claim propagates to every adopting repo rather than living only here.

FIX: correct the line to say spec.status executes command targets by default and that
--no-run-commands suppresses it. While in the file, audit the sibling task descriptions in the same
list for the same class of claim.

PROVENANCE: surfaced while grading specled_-bg5.3 (epic specled_-i4x), whose deliverable is
docs/security.md — the document positioned to correct this belief. Its first draft made the SAME
error (naming only spec.check as executing by default) and was bounced for it. This ticket is the
scaffolding half, kept separate because priv/** was Out of Scope for that ticket.

title: [BUG] Scaffolded SKILL.md.eex calls mix spec.status "Read-only." — it executes repo-authored shell by default
